content: Oral Suspension: Administer 400,000 to 600,000 units orally every 6 hours. Swish the suspension in the mouth for several minutes before swallowing. Oral Tablets: Administer 500,000 to 1,000,000 units orally every 8 hours. Powder: Dissolve 1/8 to 1/4 teaspoon of powder (equivalent to 500,000 to 1,000,000 units) in 1/2 cup of water. Administer orally every 8 hours. Liposomal Nystatin: This formulation is used for the treatment of invasive fungal infections. Retain the suspension in the mouth for as long as possible before swallowing. Drug Interactions: 1. Nystatin reduces the effectiveness of allogeneic cultured keratinocytes and fibroblasts in bovine collagen. This interaction is contraindicated. If exposed to topical antibiotics, thoroughly irrigate the wound with saline and allow an appropriate wash-out period before applying products like Gintuit. 2. Nystatin decreases the effects of Saccharomyces boulardii through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Avoid co-administration or consider alternative therapies. 3. Systemic or oral antifungals may reduce the activity of probiotics. Monitor closely. 4. Co-administration of nystatin with voclosporin may increase the toxicity of either drug due to nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be closely monitored. 5. Combining nystatin with drugs associated with nephrotoxicity increases the risk of acute or chronic kidney damage. This combination is contraindicated. Adverse Effects: Common side effects include diarrhea, nausea, stomach pain, vomiting, and contact dermatitis. Rare but serious reactions include Stevens-Johnson syndrome and hypersensitivity reactions. Discontinue therapy if irritation or sensitization occurs during use. Contraindications: Nystatin is not suitable for systemic mycoses. Use with caution during pregnancy (Category C) and lactation, as it is unknown if the drug is excreted in breast milk. Mechanism of Action: Nystatin binds to sterols in the fungal cell membrane, altering its permeability and causing leakage of cellular contents. It has poor oral absorption and is excreted unchanged in the feces. Onset of Action: Symptom relief for oral candidiasis typically occurs within 24 to 72 hours. Storage: Store at room temperature. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed. Properly discard expired or unused medication. Usage Instructions: For topical use only. Clean and thoroughly dry the affected area before application. Apply the medication to the affected skin as directed by your doctor, usually 2 to 3 times daily. Use enough powder to lightly coat the affected area and some surrounding skin. Wash your hands after application unless treating the hands. Do not wrap, cover, or bandage the treated area unless directed by your doctor. Use the medication regularly to achieve the best results. Complete the full prescribed course, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not double the dose. Overdose: If someone overdoses and exhibits serious symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call emergency services (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center immediately (1-800-222-1222 in the U.S. or 1-844-764-7669 in Canada). Precautions: Inform your doctor if you are allergic to nystatin or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other issues. Use during pregnancy only when clearly needed. Consult your doctor regarding breastfeeding. Important Note: This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information tailored to your specific health needs.
